A royal order, a jailed former prime minister, and a dispute over who has the final say. Malaysia’s king has warned the government not to challenge his authority in Najib Razak’s transfer to house arrest. Razak was due to leave prison after his party paid a $12m fine as part of the conditions of his royal pardon. Directed by Ali Najimi, the play has Amir Saeed Afshar, Ensieh Shafiee, and Mahboubeh Zarkesh in the cast. It was first performed in 1951. Since 1957, it has been in permanent showing at Paris' Théâtre de la Huchette, on an Ionesco double-bill with “The Bald Soprano”. The play is regarded as an important work in the "Theater of the Absurd". The play takes place in the office and dining room of a small French flat. The Professor, a man of 50 to 60, is expecting a new Pupil (aged 18). The Professor's Maid, a stout, red-faced woman of 40 to 50, worries about the Professor's health. As the absurd and nonsensical lesson progresses, the Professor grows more and more angry with what he perceives as the Pupil's ignorance, and the Pupil becomes more and more quiet and meek. Even her health begins to deteriorate, and what starts as a toothache develops into her entire body aching. At the climax of the play, after a long bout of non sequiturs (which are frequently used in Ionesco's plays), the Professor stabs and murders the Pupil. The play ends with the Maid greeting a new Pupil, taking the play full circle, back to the beginning. TEHRAN – The Iranian Artists Forum (IAF) in Tehran will screen “There Will Be Blood,” a 2007 American epic period drama film co-produced, written, and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, on Monday. The 158-minute movie will be shown at 5 p.m. at the Nasseri Hall of the IAF and will be followed by a review session in the presence of film critic Mehrzad Danesh, journalist Alireza Bahrami, and cultural activist Reza Mirmehrabi. It is loosely based on the 1927 novel “Oil!” by Upton Sinclair and stars Daniel Day-Lewis, Paul Dano, Kevin J. O'Connor, Ciarán Hinds, and Dillon Freasier. The film follows silver miner-turned-oilman Daniel Plainview (Day-Lewis) as he embarks on a ruthless quest for wealth during the Californian oil boom in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Critics see the film as a commentary on the nature of capitalism and greed, and its inherent national presence in America. Others have noted themes of faith, religion, and family. It received acclaim from critics, with praise for the cinematography, Anderson's direction and screenplay, music, and performances of Day-Lewis and Dano. The National Board of Review, the American Film Institute, and the National Society of Film Critics named it one of the top-ten films of 2007. The film was nominated for eight awards at the 80th Academy Awards, winning two (Best Actor for Day-Lewis and Best Cinematography for Elswit) and received numerous other accolades. Harrison was announced as the winner at a ceremony in London on Monday beating five other shortlisted authors to claim the £50,000 (approximately₹62 lakh) award. His novel, a dystopian satire set in a post-apocalyptic Britain, was selected unanimously by the judging panel chaired by historian and classicist Mary Beard. Harrison breaks the previous age record held by Canadian author Margaret Atwood, who was 79 when she jointly won the Booker Prize in 2019 for The Testaments. Atwood shared that year's award with British writer Bernardine Evaristo, who won for Girl, Woman, Other. The 2026 award also recognises Harrison's writing career, which spans six decades.
